Riftbound: Origins Card Errata

Riftbound: Origins Card Errata

The first batch of Riftbound cards errata for Origins.

Rules and Releases2025-10-28T01:00:00.000Z

[Download Card Errata]

Hey Riftbounders! We’re sharing a recap of all the card errata for Riftbound: Origins. If you’re new to TCGs or Riftbound is your first TCG, card errata is any updates to card text usually for clarity and sometimes a goof like a typo. If you’re a seasoned TCG player, you might be already diving into the PDF above.

With Origins being our first set, it has more than its fair share of errata, most of it focused on rules clarity and consistency. We expect to issue very little “day zero” errata for future sets. Most of these card errata updates have already been shared through updates in our Core Rules FAQ, so there shouldn’t be too many surprises in there. A few cards that were in the FAQ have received slightly different wordings than previously announced, and there are three cards in this file that weren’t in the FAQ.

This is also a good time to reiterate our philosophy behind card errata. Changes from printed wordings add friction to your gameplay experience, and we don’t issue them lightly. And unlike a digital game, we don’t issue “patches” for game balance reasons. Where printed card wordings created unintended gameplay, were ambiguous about their function, or didn’t quite work in our updated rules, that’s where we’ve chosen to issue errata. The majority of the errata here doesn’t change how these cards work in regular gameplay situations; rather, it clarifies their function and shores it up against edge cases and rules oddities.

We’re heads down on the Riftbound: Origins English Launch (soonTM) and designing many sets to come, so give us some time as we work to update the Card Gallery or add another database resource to note the official language of the cards. Currently, card errata is not planned to be included on any future restocks of Riftbound: Origins or potential localizations of the cards. We’ll keep you all posted if that changes though!

With the recent update to Core Rules along with our Core Rules Patch Notes plus the final piece of the Trinity Force with the Card Errata, the Core Rules FAQ is now obsolete and will be retired on November 4, 2025.

Now, that we have that out of the way, let’s dive into the Riftbound: Origins Card Errata:

We’ve got some fresh card errata for you today, covering cards from both Origins and Spiritforged. If you’re just starting Riftbound, or new to TCGs, card errata refers to any updates to card text after a card was printed. We do this to make cards more easily understood and to clarify how they work within the rules of the game.

You can find the card errata in the above PDF, or in the text below. If you’re hungry for a deep dive into our philosophy about errata or why these changes were made, check out our Riftbound Spiritforged FAQ, which goes into greater detail about these changes.

▲

Announcements2026-07-23T16:00:00.000Z

Hey Riftbounders!

We’ve got some fresh card errata for you today, covering cards from Spiritforged, Unleashed and Vendetta. If you’re just starting Riftbound, or new to TCGs, card errata refers to any updates to card text after a card was printed. We do this to make cards more easily understood and to clarify how they work within the rules of the game.

You can find the card errata in the above PDF, or in the text below.

Spiritforged Cards

Draven, Vanquisher

[NEW TEXT] 

When I win a combat, play a Gold gear token exhausted.

When I attack or defend, you may pay [C] to give me +2 [M] this turn.

▲

[OLD TEXT]

When I win a combat, play a Gold gear token exhausted.

When I attack or defend, you may pay [C]. If you do, give me +2 [M] this turn.

Emperor’s Dais

[NEW TEXT] 

When you conquer here, you may pay [1] and return a unit you control here to its owner's hand to play a 2 [M] Sand Soldier unit token here.

▲

[OLD TEXT]

When you conquer here, you may pay [1] and return a unit you control here to its owner's hand. If you do, play a 2 [M] Sand Soldier unit token here.

Fizz, Trickster

[NEW TEXT] 

When you play me, you may play a spell from your trash with Energy cost no more than [3], ignoring its Energy cost. Then recycle it. (You must still pay its Power cost.)

▲

[OLD TEXT]

When you play me, you may play a spell from your trash with Energy cost no more than [3], ignoring its Energy cost. Recycle that spell after you play it. (You must still pay its Power cost.)

Unleashed Cards

Diana, Lunari

[NEW TEXT] 

When a showdown begins here, you may pay [1] to [Predict], then reveal the top card of your Main Deck. If it's a spell, draw it. (To Predict, look at the top card of your Main Deck. You may recycle it.)

▲

[OLD TEXT]

When a showdown begins here, you may pay [1]. If you do, [Predict], then reveal the top card of your Main Deck. If it's a spell, draw it. (To Predict, look at the top card of your Main Deck. You may recycle it.)

Stalking Wolf

[NEW TEXT] 

[Ambush] (You may play me as a [Reaction] to a battlefield where you have units.)

As an additional cost to play me, kill a Bird, Cat, Dog, or Poro you control. You may [Ambush] me to its battlefield, even if you don't have other units there.

▲

[OLD TEXT]

[Ambush] (You may play me as a [Reaction] to a battlefield where you have units.)

As an additional cost to play me, kill a Bird, Cat, Dog, or Poro you control. You may play me to its battlefield (even if you don't have other units there).

Vendetta Cards

Astral Heron

[NEW TEXT] 

When you play your first card each turn, if I'm at a battlefield, the next card you play this turn costs [2][A][A] less.

▲

[OLD TEXT]

When you play your first card each turn, if I'm at a battlefield, your next card costs [2][A][A] less.

Gangplank, Naval

[NEW TEXT] 

[Empower] [C][C] ([C][C]: Empower me. Use only if not Empowered.)

[Empowered][>] If a spell or ability that chooses me would stun me, give me -[M], or return me to hand, give me +3 [M] this turn instead.

▲

[OLD TEXT]

[Empower] [C][C] ([C][C]: Empower me. Use only if not Empowered.)

[Empowered][>] If a spell or ability that chooses me would stun me, give me -[M], or return me to hand, give me +3 [M] instead.

Resonating Strike

[NEW TEXT] 

[Hidden] (Hide now for [A] to react with later for [0].)

[Reaction] (Play any time, even before spells and abilities resolve.)

Choose a battlefield you control and a unit you control at a different location. Move that unit to that battlefield and give it +2 [S] this turn.

▲

[OLD TEXT]

[Hidden] (Hide now for [A] to react with later for [0].)

[Reaction] (Play on your turn or in showdowns.)
